rationale: Two live default-selection paths remain inconsistent with persisted status and public selectability, and a new module misses a documented code-quality requirement. A pre-existing bulk status validation gap is deferred; a static startup enum concern was filtered as unreachable, and two pre-existing commit subjects are deferred though the standards audit still marks commit-format partial. Three findings require fixes; the UI acceptance row is reviewed separately.

business_review.item: AC-1 Admin read, set, replace, clear and authorization
business_review.notes: Admin routes and singleton repository implement the operations.

business_review.item: AC-2 Validate currently selectable model or auto-router
business_review.notes: Cached LiteLLM status can be stale after an admin status update.

business_review.item: AC-3 Keep invalidated choice and use valid fallback
business_review.notes: Stale LiteLLM status can leave an invalidated choice effective.

business_review.item: AC-4 Consistent internal and public resolution
business_review.notes: Public category endpoint can pick a deprecated category model.

business_review.item: AC-5 One effective global flag; retain other categories
business_review.notes: Catalog metadata is projected without mutating source.
Public default can nominate an unselectable choice.

business_review.item: AC-7 Admin UI and Help display

business_review.notes: Singleton persistence and model projections are present.

business_review.item: Database outage preserves known invalid status
business_review.notes: Last successful status cache is reused.

standards_review.notes: The new EPMCDME-15077 subjects follow the documented ticket-prefixed format, but two subjects already in the review range do not: status-persistence-api: add per-task implementation reports and contract-questions note; status-persistence-api: add planning artifacts.

The new backend modules have explicit function annotations and Apache headers, but src/codemie/rest_api/models/admin_global_default_api.py omits from __future__ import annotations, which the code-quality guide asks for in new modules.

The new admin GET, PUT, and DELETE endpoints use the central authenticate and admin_access_only dependencies; the new persistence code uses SQLAlchemy expressions and does not log credentials or normalize untrusted input before validation.

findings.title: Add required future annotations import
findings.problem: The new API model module omits from __future__ import annotations, which the repository code-quality guide requires in new Python modules.
findings.impact: The new module violates a documented blocking source convention.
findings.recommendation: Add from __future__ import annotations after the license header.

findings.title: Exclude unselectable public defaults
findings.problem: _default_for_category chooses any visible category flag and falls back to the first choice. Deprecated models remain visible; include_all also exposes disabled models. Router projections lose source status, so a deprecated router can be selected too.
findings.impact: GET /v1/default_models and its category route may return a model users cannot select, contrary to the internal resolver and the approved user-scoped default contract.
findings.recommendation: Choose only selectable entries, using source status before router projection where necessary; return no default when the user's catalog has no selectable choice.

findings.title: Refresh cached LiteLLM status
findings.problem: get_all_llm_model_info returns the initialized LiteLLM list without remerging persisted status. Admin status endpoints only update the database, so the cached model retains its prior status after a disable or deprecation.
findings.impact: An admin can save, retain, or serve a disabled model as the effective global default until the LiteLLM catalog reloads.
findings.recommendation: Refresh or update persisted status on the active LiteLLM catalog before validation and default resolution, including after status writes; preserve the last successful override during database outages.
